papers.title: Learning from What You Retrieve: Online RL Fine-Tuning for Semantic Retrieval
papers.summary: In large-scale e-commerce retrieval, dual-encoder retrievers are optimized for contrastive similarity, whereas downstream rerankers capture finer-grained relevance preferences; this objective mismatch limits end-to-end retrieval quality. Reinforcement Learning offers a way to use reward-model feedback for retriever adaptation, but we observe that standard policy-gradient updates can degrade embedding geometry, especially when the document index must remain frozen due to industrial constraints. papers.title: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback: A Statistical Perspective
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) has emerged as a central framework for aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences. Despite its practical success, RLHF raises fundamental statistical questions because it relies on noisy, subjective, and heterogeneous feedback to learn reward models and optimize policies. This review provides a statistical perspective on RLHF, focusing primarily on LLM alignment. We introduce the main components of RLHF, including supervised fine-tuning, reward modeling, and policy optimization, and relate them to familiar statistical concepts

papers.title: EVOL: Simulator-Guided Evolutionary Expert Synthesis for Deployment-Free Learning Path Recommendation
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) for learning path recommendation (LPR) faces two coupled obstacles. First, the policy must commit to a sequence of L concepts without intermediate feedback, producing a combinatorial search space that grows super-exponentially with L and provides reward only at the final step. Second, expert learning paths would be the natural cure for sparse-reward RL, but they do not exist in educational data, because student logs record what learners did, not what they should have done. papers.title: Graph-GRPO: Dependency-Aware Credit Assignment for Generative E-commerce Search Relevance
papers.summary: Search relevance modeling is a core task in e-commerce search systems, assessing how well a user query matches candidate products. Rather than relying on a single holistic matching signal, relevance judgment often requires structured reasoning over query understanding, product understanding, and facet-level matching. With large language models (LLMs), this process is increasingly formulated as chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning and optimized with reinforcement learning (RL). papers.title: Distinguishing artificial intelligence from robotic execution in total knee arthroplasty: a narrative review and evidence map
papers.summary: Abstract Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine-learning methods are increasingly discussed in relation to robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (TKA). However, robotic assistance, computer navigation, and AI-based prediction represent distinct functions that are often conflated under the single label “AI-assisted robotic TKA,” obscuring the state of evidence for each. papers.title: Reinforcement learning enables autonomous microrobot navigation and intervention in simulated blood capillaries
papers.summary: Abstract Autonomous microrobots navigating biological vasculature could enable targeted drug delivery and thrombolysis, yet training control policies for physiologically complex environments remains an open challenge. Prior reinforcement learning (RL) studies of microrobotic navigation have largely used idealized geometries lacking realistic flow in confined branching, and dense cellular obstacles. papers.title: Run Time Assurance Filter Framework for Collision Avoidance of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Using Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: In recent years, Reinforcement Learning (RL) has been increasingly applied to the collision avoidance systems of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) due to its high performance in complex tasks and relatively low online computational cost. Despite these advantages, the lack of interpretability in RL and decision-making processes poses significant challenges to safety verification, which severely limits the practical deployment of RL-based autonomous flight systems in safety-critical scenarios. papers.title: From Individual Learning to Market Equilibrium: Correcting Structural and Parametric Biases in RL Simulations of Economic Models
papers.summary: Abstract Applying Reinforcement Learning (RL) to economic modeling reveals a fundamental tension: standard RL agents do not behave as competitive price-takers. While macroeconomic models typically assume agents take aggregate conditions as given, a naive single-agent RL algorithm learns to internalize its impact on the environment, effectively exerting market power. papers.title: ViSalRec: Visual and Saliency-Informed Reward Augmentation for Sequential Recommender Systems
papers.summary: In Reinforcement Learning (RL)-based sequential recommendation, offline training often reduces user feedback to sparse binary rewards, weakening credit assignment and limiting policy optimisation. In visual recommendation settings, user choices are also shaped by product appearance, visual attention, and semantic impressions, which provide preference cues that binary outcomes cannot capture. papers.summary: A robotic system that integrates prestressing-steel strand cutting with automated surface roughening was developed to address the high labor cost, harsh working conditions, and poor quality consistency encountered in anchor-hole operations for prefabricated box girders. papers.title: Hakka Kitchen: Engagement with Culinary Cultural Heritage Through Immersive Game Play
papers.summary: Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) experiences are difficult to share with the public because they are essentially processes that rely on physical interactions with embodied, tacit, and situated phenomena in specific cultural contexts. We consume non-interactive media such as videos and books to learn about culinary ICH experiences, but they do not allow us to grasp actual interactive procedures that embody the cultural knowledge. papers.title: Criminal Liability in the Age of Autonomous Systems
papers.summary: The rapid integration of autonomous systems into everyday life has transformed multiple sectors, including transportation, healthcare, manufacturing, defense, and public administration. These systems—powered by artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, robotics, and advanced sensors—are capable of making decisions with minimal or no human intervention. papers.title: Design of a Gantry-Type Intelligent Grasping Device for Logistics Warehousing Based on MaixCam
papers.summary: Traditional warehousing suffers from low efficiency, high manual error rates, substantial labor costs, and complex deployment, while existing sorting devices remain poorly adaptable for small- and medium-sized operations. To address these issues, this paper presents an intelligent gantry-type grasping device for logistics warehousing based on the MaixCam. The device integrates mechanical design, computer vision, and electronic control. papers.title: Spectral 3D computer vision: A survey of acquisition, representations, learning, and applications
papers.summary: Spectral 3D computer vision combines wavelength-resolved measurements with geometric information to support material-aware reconstruction, perception, and scene analysis. However, the literature remains fragmented across hyperspectral and multispectral sensing, cross-spectral depth and pose estimation, spectral point clouds, LiDAR–hyperspectral fusion, and neural scene representations. papers.title: Inter-trial intervals bias reinforcement learning in humans
papers.summary: Although we know humans attempt to maximize reward per unit time when foraging, it remains unclear how the common practice of varying waiting time via inter-trial intervals (ITI) impacts reinforcement learning. papers.title: FBOmission
papers.summary: Preprocessed, segmented EEG data (−700 to 1500 ms, 0.1–30 Hz, no baseline correction) of 48 participants performing a probabilistic reinforcement learning task with omissions of rewards and losses, merged with trial-wise behavioural data and model-derived prediction errors. Data underlie Weber, C., Jocham, G., Bellebaum, C. (under review) Cortical prediction error responses to reward and loss omission; please cite this publication when using the data.
